section: Right to Information Act 2005 - structure, exemptions, amendments and issues
subsections: RTI Act sections and Section 8 exemptions
Time limits - reply, life and liberty, third party, appeals

accepted.s: Which one of the following is included in the definition of “information” under Section 2(f) of the Right to Information Act, 2005?
o: Records, documents, e-mails, opinions, samples and electronic data
Only opinions expressed by public officials
accepted.x: Section 2(f) includes records, documents, e-mails, opinions, advice, press releases, circulars, orders, logbooks, contracts, reports, papers, samples, models and electronic data.
accepted.tq: Use the exact statutory definition instead of narrowing the term to paper records.
accepted.sec: RTI Act sections and Section 8 exemptions

accepted.s:
With reference to the Right to Information Act, 2005, consider the following statements:
1. A body substantially financed or controlled by the government may be a public authority.
2. A body established by a government notification may be a public authority.
3. Only bodies created directly by the Constitution can be public authorities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct under Section 2(h). Statement 3 is false because public authorities also include bodies established by law or government notification and substantially financed or controlled by government.
accepted.tq: Split the definition into its alternative categories and reject the word “only”.
accepted.sec: RTI Act sections and Section 8 exemptions

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the right to information under Section 2(j) of the Right to Information Act, 2005?
o: Inspection of work, documents and records
Compelling a public authority to create new information
accepted.x: Section 2(j) permits inspection, taking notes or extracts, obtaining certified copies and taking certified samples. It does not require a public authority to create information that it does not hold.
accepted.tq: Distinguish access to existing records from a demand to generate new information.
accepted.sec: RTI Act sections and Section 8 exemptions

accepted.s: Which Section of the Right to Information Act, 2005 provides that every citizen shall have the right to information?
accepted.x: Section 3 declares that all citizens shall have the right to information, subject to the provisions of the Act.
accepted.tq: Test the precise section number rather than the broader subject of the provision.
accepted.sec: RTI Act sections and Section 8 exemptions

accepted.s:
Under Section 6 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, an application for information may be made in which of the following ways and languages?
1. By post, in person or through e-mail
2. In Hindi, English or the official language of the area
3. Only after stating the reasons for seeking the information
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Applications may be submitted by post, in person or electronically and may be made in Hindi, English or the local official language. Under Section 6(2), the applicant need not give reasons for seeking information, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Catch the reversed requirement that an applicant must disclose reasons.
accepted.sec: RTI Act sections and Section 8 exemptions

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II relating to provisions of the Right to Information Act, 2005:

List-I (Section)
A. Section 5
B. Section 9
C. Section 12
D. Section 15

List-II (Subject)
1. Constitution of the Central Information Commission
2. Constitution of the State Information Commission
3. Designation of Public Information Officers and Assistant Public Information Officers
4. Rejection where disclosure would infringe copyright of a person other than the State

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Section 5 concerns PIOs and APIOs; Section 9 concerns copyright belonging to a person other than the State; Sections 12 and 15 concern the CIC and SIC respectively.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure statutory pair and eliminate codes that disturb it.
accepted.sec: RTI Act sections and Section 8 exemptions

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with Section 8(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005?
o: Commercial confidence and trade secrets — Section 8(1)(a)
Information held in a fiduciary relationship — Section 8(1)(e)
Information from a foreign government in confidence — Section 8(1)(j)
accepted.x: Section 8(1)(e) covers information available to a person in his fiduciary relationship. Commercial confidence and trade secrets fall under clause (d), foreign-government information under clause (f), and personal information under clause (j).
accepted.tq: Discriminate between neighbouring clauses by matching each exemption with its exact letter.
accepted.sec: RTI Act sections and Section 8 exemptions

accepted.s: Under Section 8(2) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, information covered by an exemption may be disclosed when
o: the information is more than five years old
the public interest in disclosure outweighs the harm to the protected interests
the applicant is a citizen for more than five years
the information is requested through an APIO
accepted.x: Section 8(2) permits disclosure where the public interest in disclosure outweighs the harm to the protected interests, including in cases involving the Official Secrets Act.
accepted.tq: Apply the public-interest override rather than treating exemptions as absolute.
accepted.sec: RTI Act sections and Section 8 exemptions

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Section 8(3) of the Right to Information Act, 2005:
1. Exempt information is generally disclosable after twenty years.
2. Cabinet deliberations are excluded from the twenty-year disclosure rule.
3. Information concerning foreign relations is excluded from the twenty-year disclosure rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The twenty-year rule does not apply to cabinet deliberations, information affecting security, strategic or economic interests, foreign relations and incitement to an offence.
accepted.tq: Look for statutory exceptions to a general time rule instead of assuming it is universal.
accepted.sec: RTI Act sections and Section 8 exemptions

accepted.s: Disclosure of information may be rejected under Section 9 of the Right to Information Act, 2005 when such disclosure would
o: disclose information older than twenty years
reveal any information held by a public authority
infringe the copyright of a person other than the State
accepted.x: Section 9 permits rejection where access would involve infringement of copyright subsisting in a person other than the State.
accepted.tq: Separate the copyright-based ground under Section 9 from the security and privacy exemptions under Section 8.
accepted.sec: RTI Act sections and Section 8 exemptions

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the organisations generally covered by the exemption under Section 24 and the Second Schedule of the Right to Information Act, 2005?
accepted.x: The IB, R&AW and CRPF are among the intelligence and security organisations covered by Section 24. The Central Information Commission is the appellate information body and is not a Section 24 exempt organisation.
accepted.tq: Identify the odd institutional category instead of confusing an exempt security body with the appellate authority.
accepted.sec: RTI Act sections and Section 8 exemptions

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Section 24 of the Right to Information Act, 2005 is correct?
o: Information relating to corruption and human-rights violations is not excluded from disclosure merely because it is held by a listed organisation.
It applies only to organisations created after 2005.
It excludes all information held by intelligence and security organisations without exception.
It removes the jurisdiction of the Information Commission in every case involving a security organisation.
accepted.x: Section 24 generally excludes listed intelligence and security organisations, but information concerning corruption and human-rights violations remains subject to disclosure under the specified conditions.
accepted.tq: Test the exception to a broad exclusion and reject absolute wording such as “all” and “without exception”.
accepted.sec: RTI Act sections and Section 8 exemptions

accepted.s: The Central Bureau of Investigation was added to the exempt organisations under the Second Schedule of the Right to Information Act in
accepted.x: The Central Bureau of Investigation was added to the Second Schedule in 2011, subject to the statutory exceptions relating to corruption and human-rights violations.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive amendment year rather than the year of enactment of the Act.
accepted.sec: RTI Act sections and Section 8 exemptions

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Section 11 — Third-party information
2. Section 19 — Appeals
3. Section 20 — Penalties on Public Information Officers
4. Section 22 — Overriding effect over the Official Secrets Act, 1923

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. Sections 11, 19, 20 and 22 respectively deal with third-party information, appeals, penalties and the overriding effect of the RTI Act.
accepted.tq: Check each section–subject pair and use the comprehensive option only when every pair is accurate.
accepted.sec: RTI Act sections and Section 8 exemptions

accepted.s:
Arrange the following stages of an RTI appeal process in the correct chronological order:
A. Second appeal to the Central or State Information Commission
B. Application for information to the Public Information Officer
C. First appeal to the First Appellate Authority
D. Decision or expiry of the period prescribed for the first application

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The applicant first approaches the PIO, waits for the decision or expiry of the prescribed period, files the first appeal, and may thereafter file a second appeal before the Information Commission.
accepted.tq: Fix the initial application and final second appeal, then place the first appeal between them.
accepted.sec: Time limits - reply, life and liberty, third party, appeals

accepted.s: An application for information is submitted through an Assistant Public Information Officer. Within what maximum period should the normal response ordinarily be provided?
accepted.x: An application routed through an APIO carries an additional five days over the normal thirty-day period, making the period thirty-five days.
accepted.tq: Add the APIO forwarding period to the ordinary thirty-day limit.
accepted.sec: Time limits - reply, life and liberty, third party, appeals

accepted.s: Where the information sought concerns the life or liberty of a person, the Public Information Officer is required to provide it within
accepted.x: Requests concerning the life or liberty of a person must be answered within forty-eight hours.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the special urgent limit from the normal thirty-day period.
accepted.sec: Time limits - reply, life and liberty, third party, appeals

accepted.s: The time limit for dealing with information relating to a third party under Section 11 of the Right to Information Act is generally
accepted.x: Third-party information cases carry a period of forty days because the third party must be given an opportunity to make a representation.
accepted.tq: Do not substitute the ordinary PIO period for the special third-party period.
accepted.sec: Time limits - reply, life and liberty, third party, appeals

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding appeals under the Right to Information Act, 2005:
1. The first appeal is ordinarily filed within thirty days.
2. The First Appellate Authority may decide the first appeal within thirty days or, for recorded reasons, within an extended period not exceeding forty-five days.
3. A second appeal to the Central or State Information Commission is ordinarily filed within ninety days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The first appeal is due within thirty days, its decision period may extend to forty-five days with reasons, and the second appeal is ordinarily filed within ninety days.
accepted.tq: Separate the filing period from the decision period and then identify the longer second-appeal limit.
accepted.sec: Time limits - reply, life and liberty, third party, appeals

accepted.s: In a case involving a human-rights allegation against an organisation exempt under Section 24, information is to be provided within
o: 45 days, with the approval of the Information Commission
40 days, after approval of the Public Information Officer
90 days, after approval of the Central Government
accepted.x: For human-rights allegations involving a Section 24 exempt organisation, disclosure may be made within forty-five days and requires the approval of the Information Commission.
accepted.tq: Match the special case with both its exceptional time limit and approving authority.
accepted.sec: Time limits - reply, life and liberty, third party, appeals
